3. Changed files
- `plugins/pipeline-core/lib/governance-event-store.mjs`: new `assertRestrictedChildPrivate` (win32: create -> `hardenWindowsPrivateDirectory`, existing -> `assessWindowsPrivatePath`; POSIX: the old mode check, same code and message); `restrictedRecordsRoot` and `restrictedAuxiliaryRoot` use it and derive `created` from the `mkdir({recursive})` return value.

4. Deliberately not changed
- Tests, `hardened-private-directory.mjs`, every other production file, and the D1 mode-unrecorded host class: untouched as briefed.
- The two helpers keep no injectable `io` seam (unlike `assertRestrictedRoot`): they are not exported and tests are forbidden in this slice, so a seam would be untested surface. The win32 branch is exercised by the real native PowerShell assessor in `:1138`.
- `assertRestrictedRoot` still hardens an already-existing store root when called with `create: true` (flag-based, not creation-based). Out of scope; the new helpers are creation-based instead (see deviations).

5. Deviations / judgment calls (flagged for the Elephant, each a one-token flip)
- Typed code: the briefing says "otherwise the existing typed refusal". I kept `GES-RESTRICTED-PERMISSIONS`, the only code the briefing names for these two helpers, so POSIX and win32 share one typed refusal. The alternative `GES-RESTRICTED-WINDOWS-ASSURANCE` (what `assertRestrictedRoot` throws, and what `:1277-1287` pin for the root) would be a one-token change. The win32 message now appends the assessor's status and reason (path-free per Ruling 154); the POSIX message is byte-identical.
- "A root this call creates is hardened": implemented literally via the `mkdir` return value, not via the `create` flag. Consequence: `put` hardens `records` only on the call that creates it and later calls (and `restrictedStatus`, `findRestrictedIdempotency`) assess it. This costs one PowerShell assessment per `records` access on win32.
- The capture headers record `head: b9040293...`, not the briefed candidate `f06975126`: HEAD advanced under concurrent work. I did not touch the module before the edit; its pre-edit `git status` entry was clean.

- Independent Critic review: pending (S class; only the Elephant dispatches it).
- Not verified: `:1138` and the rest of the file pass natively and under WSL, but no other suite that imports the restricted helpers was run (single targeted test file, as briefed).
- The dispatch record was finalized with a scratch script (`finalize.mjs`) in one write; the commit SHA was taken from the commit output.
